newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudis plan $50 mln firm to invest in C. Asia.
newsitem.headline: Saudis plan $50 mln firm to invest in C. Asia.

text.p: A group of Saudi Arabian investors plan to form a $50 million firm to promote investment in the former Soviet Central Asian republics, the Arab News newspaper said on Monday.

The Saudi newspaper said the group would meet in Jeddah later this month "to work out details leading to the formation of an international company to promote investments in the former Soviet Moslem republics."
The move followed investment conferences held in some Islamic republics sponsored by the Jeddah-based Islamic Development Bank (IDB) last September.
The newspaper said shareholders of the new company held their first meeting at the IDB headquarters last week.
"Registration of the company could take place either in the Virgin Islands or the state of Bahrain," the English-language daily said.
Former Saudi deputy minister of commerce Abdul-Rahman al-Zamil had been appointed chairman of the new company.
"Saudi businessmen are interested in doing business in Central Asian republics but prefer to do it collectively," Zamil said.

"The region could serve as a potential market for Saudi products looking for international outlets and provide Saudi businessmen with the opportunity to build their own factories in these states," he added.
